name: North Noise (reverse sigmas with injected noise)
plain: An unsampler that walks flipped sigmas from low to high, but begins by passing strong Gaussian as the noise argument. It mixes model-driven inversion with an initial noise bump, optionally masked.
math: ε ~ N(0,I)·strength (default 3), mask multiplies ε if given. σ' = reverse(σ[start..end+1]) + [1e-4]. Runs KSampler.sample(noise=ε, sigmas=σ').
label: from code
surprise: Default strength is 3.0×, and the sigma list ends with 1e-4 appended even though flipped sigmas ascend.
